requiredDocumentFields.label: Buyer reference / order reference
requiredDocumentFields.why: The vendored NLCIUS delta's own BR-NL-2 (`formats/vendored/nl/si-ubl-2.0-nlcius-preprocessed.sch`) requires either a buyer reference (cbc:BuyerReference, BT-10) or an order reference (cac:OrderReference/cbc:ID, BT-13) — but ONLY when the INVOICING company (the supplier) is itself established in the Netherlands (the rule's own `[$s]` context predicate, `supplierIsNL`): unlike Germany's Leitweg-ID (BR-DE-15, unconditional for every seller — see `country-fields/data/de.json`'s own header), every NLCIUS BR-NL-* rule in the vendored delta is gated this way. Left `required: false` (an informational hint, never a hard block) for exactly that reason: a non-Dutch company invoicing this Dutch government client will never trigger BR-NL-2 at all, so forcing this field on them would assert something the vendored rule itself does not.

provenance.sourceText: eInvoicing Country Factsheet — the Netherlands (European Commission, Digital Building Blocks, eInvoicing space, page 467108895): "NLCIUS is a customised version of the semantic model of the core elements of an electronic invoice, defined in EN 16931-1:2017, for the Netherlands." On the network: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is cited "with specific rules for the Netherlands" — i.e. NLCIUS itself, carried over the Peppol network exactly like Germany's XRechnung is (`b2g-routing/data/de.json`'s own ADDENDUM). CustomizationID and the BR-NL-1..35 rules themselves are read VERBATIM from the OFFICIAL vendored source, never the factsheet's own prose: peppolautoriteit-nl/validation (Peppol Autoriteit NL / Stichting Simplerinvoicing), tag `2025-11-27`, `schematron/si-ubl-2.0.sch`'s own fatal `[SI-V20-INV-R000]` assert (`starts-with(cbc:CustomizationID, 'urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:fdc:nen.nl:nlcius:v1.0')`) and `schematron/si-ubl-2.0/si-ubl-2.0-nlcius.sch`'s own BR-NL-1 ("the supplier MUST provide either a KVK or OIN number for its legal entity identifier ... with schemeID 0106 or 0190") and BR-NL-10 (the same, for the customer, when the customer is ALSO in the Netherlands) — see `formats/vendored/nl/si-ubl-2.0-nlcius-preprocessed.sch`'s own header for the full provenance (LICENSE.txt MIT, Copyright (c) 2017 Stichting Simplerinvoicing, copied alongside).

rule.notes:
MANDANT DECISION (2026-09-05, root TODO "NLCIUS vendorable") — this REOPENS `B2G_COVERAGE.md`'s 2026-09-02 "🟡 pas livrable" verdict for the Netherlands, whose ONLY cited blocker was "NLCIUS ... non vendorable": the NL audit agent had already established the official repo ships it under an MIT LICENSE.txt, and the mandant approved vendoring it — see `formats/vendored/nl/si-ubl-2.0-nlcius-preprocessed.sch`'s own header for the tag choice (`2025-11-27`, `prerelease: false` on GitHub, over the newer-but-flagged-prerelease `2026-05-21` — both tags carry a BYTE-IDENTICAL `si-ubl-2.0-nlcius.sch`, diffed directly before choosing) and for what was, and was NOT, vendored (only the NLCIUS-specific delta — this repo's own already-vendored base EN 16931 UBL Schematron is reused, never the origin repo's own bundled copy of it). `transportId: "peppol"` and `formatSyntax: "nlcius"` are BOTH now implemented in this repo (`transports/peppol-transport.ts`, `formats/nlcius-provider.ts`) via the SAME `formatOverride` mechanism DE's own XRechnung wiring established (`documents-core.module.ts#buildTransportRegistry`'s `formatOverrides.nlcius`, `fe61e3e8`'s own precedent) — a Dutch government client therefore gets a REAL NLCIUS artifact over the SAME Peppol channel this repo already sends generic Peppol BIS through, never a silent Peppol-BIS substitute (see `peppol-transport.ts`'s own header, "THE FORMAT OVERRIDE", for why an unwired override would instead be a NAMED refusal).

A GENUINE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE FROM XRECHNUNG, read directly in the vendored `.sch`, not assumed by analogy: EVERY BR-NL-* rule in the NLCIUS delta (BR-NL-1 through BR-NL-35) is scoped to `[$s]` ("supplier is established in the Netherlands AND the document claims the NLCIUS/SI-UBL-2.0 CustomizationID") — unlike XRechnung's BR-DE-* rules, which apply to ANY seller regardless of nationality (`xrechnung-provider.ts`'s own "COUNTRY-NEUTRAL BY DESIGN" section). This is WHY `requiredClientIdentifiers` is deliberately left EMPTY here (unlike FR's own SIRET or IT's own Codice Univoco Ufficio, both unconditional): BR-NL-10 (the CUSTOMER's own KVK/OIN requirement) only fires when the INVOICING COMPANY is itself Dutch — declaring it as an unconditional required identifier on THIS client would assert something false for the (likely far more common) case of a non-Dutch seller invoicing this same Dutch government client, for whom the vendored delta enforces nothing about the customer's own identifier at all. The unconditional part of the SI-UBL-2.0 profile is only `[SI-V20-INV-R000]` (the CustomizationID itself) — carried entirely by `nlcius-provider.ts`, nothing left for this routing rule to add.

EAS NÉERLANDAIS (⚖, LU dans le `.sch` vendoré lui-même, jamais deviné) : BR-NL-1/BR-NL-10 (`formats/vendored/nl/si-ubl-2.0-nlcius-preprocessed.sch`) exigent que le `cac:PartyLegalEntity/cbc:CompanyID` (l'identifiant d'entité légale — DIFFÉRENT du `cbc:EndpointID`/BT-34/BT-49, l'adresse électronique Peppol) porte le schemeID ISO 6523 `0106` (KVK — Kamer van Koophandel) ou `0190` (OIN — Overheidsidentificatienummer, réservé aux organismes publics néerlandais). La MÊME paire est ÉGALEMENT exigée par le delta Peppol BIS GÉNÉRIQUE déjà vendoré dans ce dépôt pour un fournisseur néerlandais, `NL-R-003`/`NL-R-005` (`formats/vendored/peppol/PEPPOL-EN16931-UBL.sch:880-894`) — un fait DÉJÀ documenté, avant cette tâche, par `country-identifiers/data/nl.json`'s own note sur le KVK-nummer. `country-identifiers/data/nl.json` ne modélise QUE le KVK (schemeID `0106`) — jamais l'OIN (`0190`, réservé aux organismes publics, hors du périmètre "tout client/société" de ce catalogue) : `semantic/build-semantic-invoice.ts`'s own `LEGAL_ID_SCHEME_BY_COUNTRY` map (NOUVEAU, cette tâche) n'émet donc jamais que `0106` pour un parti néerlandais. Le `PEPPOL_ENDPOINT` du client (adresse de ROUTAGE, BT-34/BT-49 — un fait SÉPARÉ du `PartyLegalEntity/CompanyID` ci-dessus) garde sa PROPRE section dédiée sur l'écran client ("Peppol / Electronic routing", déjà `0106 — NL KVK` disponible dans son sélecteur depuis TODO_PRODUIT.md T4-b) — même raisonnement que `de.json`'s own note sur le Leitweg-ID/PEPPOL_ENDPOINT : aucun `requiredClientIdentifiers` n'est ajouté pour ce fait non plus.

LIMITE HONNÊTE, NOMMÉE : cette règle affirme que le réseau Peppol EST le canal B2G néerlandais accepté (lu sur la fiche EC) et que le CONTENU doit être NLCIUS plutôt qu'un Peppol BIS générique (même lecture, "with specific rules for the Netherlands") — elle n'affirme RIEN sur la disponibilité RÉELLE d'un point d'accès Peppol pour telle administration néerlandaise précise, ni sur son `PEPPOL_ENDPOINT` réel, qui reste un fait à saisir par l'utilisateur sur SA fiche client, jamais deviné ici. Digipoort (le portail central bas volume également cité par la fiche EC et par `B2G_COVERAGE.md`'s own row) n'est PAS implémenté dans ce dépôt et n'est PAS ce que cette règle route vers — seul le chemin Peppol/NLCIUS l'est.
